historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: nominal mid-cycle growth (terminal 2.0%). Every trailing CAGR is a cycle-phase artifact: 3-yr windows start at the 2022 crack-spread peak, 5-yr windows start at the 2020 COVID trough (FY2020 EPS -9.06 and owner FCF -936 make the 5-yr EPS/FCF CAGRs undefined). Revenue 10-yr CAGR of 3.0% (FY2015-25) is the least distorted series and supports ~2-2.5% nominal.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5-yr CAGR +7.0% vs EPS 3-yr -22.6% and revenue 5-yr +15.6%: divergence far exceeds 30%. Cause is cyclicality plus portfolio change (DCP consolidation 2022-23, WRB 100% from Oct-2025, Coastal Bend 2025, European retail sale 2025), not a growth signal. Equity CAGR is not used.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF 3-yr CAGR (-33.2%) is close to reported (-31.8%): SBC is ~0.15% of revenue and is not what drives the FCF series; the commodity cycle is. Owner FCF history 2018-25: 4,834 / 766 / -936 / 4,013 / 8,409 / 4,314 / 2,122 / 2,509; LTM Sep-26 12,138 (super-cycle peak). Annual CAGRs are unchanged from the October build: no new fiscal year has closed.

scenario_narratives.base: The diesel super-cycle peaked in Q3-2026 (realized refining margin $38/bbl, ~$8B of EBITDA in one quarter) and is fading through Q4-2026 and H1-2027 as offline capacity returns: the prompt 3:2:1 crack has fallen from ~$66 in September to ~$41 in mid-November. Realized margins settle near the ~$12/bbl seen in Q3/Q4-2025, helped modestly by permanent closures (PSX Los Angeles, Valero Benicia). Midstream reaches the guided $4.5B EBITDA run-rate by YE2027, CPChem's Golden Triangle and Ras Laffan crackers start in 2027, Renewable Fuels hovers near breakeven as credit values normalise, and capex runs above $2.5B through 2029 for Western Gateway before reverting. Mid-cycle consolidated EBITDA ~$10.4B; the windfall is captured once - Q3-2026 in net debt and buybacks already done, the tail in year 1 - and not in the terminal value.
scenario_narratives.bull: Structural rationalisation is real: global closures plus slow restarts lift the through-cycle realized refining margin to ~$15/bbl, the November crack dip proves temporary and the super-cycle runs to mid-2027, Midstream beats $4.5B with Permian volume growth, CPChem's new capacity lands into a chemicals upcycle (HDPE chain margin was 18.8c/lb in Q3-26 vs 7.6c a year earlier), and SAF/LCFS credit values keep Rodeo profitable. Mid-cycle EBITDA ~$13B. Elliott-driven portfolio discipline continues without a value-destroying break-up.
scenario_narratives.bear: Offline Russian and Middle-East barrels plus new Indian/Middle-East/Chinese capacity return in early 2027 and cracks revert to 2024 levels (~$9/bbl realized; refining adjusted EBITDA ~$1.6B), Renewable Fuels slips back to losses as credits oversupply (it lost $380M in 2025), CPChem's new crackers start into a chemicals trough, marketing margins stay squeezed (international marketing fuel margin was negative in Q1 and Q3-26), and California/EU regulation keeps squeezing the legacy footprint. Midstream (~$4.2B) is the floor. Mid-cycle EBITDA ~$7.5B, and the >50%-of-OCF payout commitment collides with a capex programme that has just been raised.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value Phillips 66 on mid-cycle owner FCF, not on the 2026 super-cycle print. LTM Sep-26 owner FCF ($12.1B) and Q3-26's ~$8B EBITDA quarter are peak-cycle; the model banks the windfall once - Q3 through lower net debt and a lower share count, the fading tail in year 1 - and capitalises a ~$10.4B mid-cycle EBITDA (anchored on the first two post-WRB, post-LA quarters at ~$12/bbl realized margins plus guided Midstream and CPChem growth). The market price still implies a mid-cycle well above that.
key_risks_to_valuation: Duration of the diesel super-cycle: each extra quarter at Q2-26 margins adds roughly $3B of EBITDA (~$6/share after tax); a quarter at Q3-26 margins roughly $5B (~$10/share)
Mid-cycle refining margin: each $1/bbl of realized margin is ~$0.78B of EBITDA per year (~785 MMbbl/yr processed at Q3-26 rates), roughly $16-19/share capitalised
Midstream $4.5B run-rate execution and any Elliott-driven separation (a SOTP crystallisation would argue for a higher blended terminal multiple than 14x)
2027+ capex: the Western Gateway uplift is not yet quantified by the company; the model adds ~$1B over three years with no associated EBITDA
Working-capital reversal as prices fall: $1.1B is deducted in the bridge; a larger unwind of the $13.5B payables book would cut further
CPChem cash retention for Golden Triangle/Ras Laffan: 9M-26 undistributed equity earnings were $952M; equity earnings are assumed to equal distributions across the cycle

inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: 390.07M common shares on the Q3-2026 10-Q cover (30-Sep-2026) plus ~1.9M incremental share-based-award shares (Q3-26 10-Q EPS note, diluted effect 1,942K). Down from 401.0M at the June anchor: 9.67M shares repurchased in Q3-26 against 0.73M issued for awards. Held FLAT going forward: SBC is fully expensed in the flows, so buybacks are the cash mechanism that keeps the count flat and are value-neutral in this model.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense $220M (XBRL); LTM proxy = FY2025. Equity-award withholding taxes are not separately disclosed on the cash-flow statement; SBC is ~0.15% of revenue so the omission is immaterial (<$0.5/share).
inputs.buyback_note: LTM Sep-2026 repurchases $3,195M (FY25 1,207 - 9M-25 933 + 9M-26 2,921). Pace stepped up sharply: $2,273M in Q3-26 alone versus $648M in H1-26, funded by the Q3 windfall ($7.3B OCF). Repurchaser: the flat count is funded. $10B authorization increase July 2026. Dividend raised to $1.33/quarter in October 2026.
inputs.fy0_basis_note: FY0 is the twelve months to 30-Sep-2026 (revenue FY25 132,376 - 9M-25 98,268 + 9M-26 134,084 = 168,192), because net debt is taken from the 30-Sep-2026 balance sheet. Q3-2026's cash generation is therefore counted once, in net debt, and NOT in year-1 flows. Projection year 1 is Oct-2026 to Sep-2027. Every later driver year is the prior (Oct-2026) dollar path time-shifted one quarter (0.75 x prior year N + 0.25 x prior year N+1), not a re-judgment.
inputs.reported_fcf_note: LTM Sep-26: OCF 15,028 (FY25 4,962 - 9M-25 2,210 + 9M-26 12,276) less capital expenditures & investments 2,670 (FY25 2,233 - 9M-25 1,551 + 9M-26 1,988) = 12,358. Owner FCF 12,138 after SBC 220. This LTM is the super-cycle peak (Q3-26 realized refining margin $38.00/bbl, composite 3:2:1 market crack $60.17, EBITDA ~$8.0B in the quarter; Q2-26 $24.08/bbl) and includes a ~$1.1B working-capital inflow in Q3. It is NOT the run-rate the projection compounds; the forward build is component-based on a mid-cycle margin.

owner_fcf_history.note: OCF - capital expenditures & investments (10-K capital spending tables: 2,639/3,873/2,920/1,860/2,194/2,418/1,859/2,233) - SBC. Levered (after interest paid ~$0.9B/yr). 2018-25 mean $3.25B on a smaller asset base (pre-DCP consolidation, pre-WRB 100%, pre-Coastal Bend). LTM Sep-26 includes ~$1.1B of working-capital inflow.

inputs.wacc_rationale: USD build. Risk-free 4.3% (10y UST), ERP 5.0%, beta ~1.15 -> cost of equity ~10.1%; pre-tax cost of debt ~5.3% (BBB+), after-tax ~4.0%; market-value weights ~88/12 (equity ~$96B, net debt $12.7B) -> ~9.3%, rounded to 9.0% because a growing ~40% of mid-cycle EBITDA is fee-based Midstream. Same WACC in all scenarios: cyclicality is charged in the scenario flows (mid-cycle normalisation + 25% bear weight), not as a WACC premium (adaptations 7f). UNCHANGED from the October build.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP: operating lease cost (~$600M/yr cash in FY2025) is already an operating expense inside EBITDA, and operating lease liabilities are EXCLUDED from net debt. Finance leases (principal ~$30M/yr) sit inside total_debt via LongTermDebtAndCapitalLeaseObligations and are not deducted from flows. One treatment per lease class, no double count.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are consolidated (pre-NCI). NCI (mainly third-party interests in consolidated Midstream entities; NCI adjusted EBITDA ~$200M/yr; NCI net income $23M in Q3-26) is charged ONCE, in the equity bridge at ~$1.7B (~8.5x NCI EBITDA; book NCI $1,172M at 30-Sep-2026). Unchanged.
inputs.equity_affiliate_treatment: CPChem (50%) and other equity affiliates enter EBITDA as reported equity earnings (the company's consolidated 'EBITDA adjusted for special items' basis, NOT the 'Adjusted EBITDA' that grosses up affiliates' proportional D&A/interest/tax). Equity earnings are assumed ~= distributions across the cycle; CPChem is currently retaining cash to fund Golden Triangle and Ras Laffan (H1-26 undistributed $600M), which is the cost of the 2027 earnings step-up modelled from year 2. Cash tax is applied to EBIT including after-tax equity earnings, a small (~$0.2B/yr) conservative overcharge.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF with mid-cycle normalisation (dcf-methods routing row 'operating company, cyclical' + owner-fcf-adaptations). UPDATE of the 2026-10-02 build on the Q3-2026 10-Q; same model, same WACC, terminal assumptions, scenario weights and mid-cycle EBITDA levels. Phillips 66 is an operating company (refining, midstream, marketing, chemicals JV), so owner-FCF is the right engine; the cyclical adaptation is that the LTM base sits at a refining super-cycle peak and is NOT extrapolated. WHAT CHANGED: (1) anchors rolled to 30-Sep-2026 - net debt 16,466 -> 12,682, diluted shares 401.0 -> 392.0, FY0 = LTM Sep-26; (2) year 1 (now Oct-26 to Sep-27) EBITDA re-judged on Q3-26 actuals and the Q4-to-date crack: base $14.0B (Q4-26 ~5.5, Q1-27 ~3.0, Q2-27 ~2.8, Q3-27 ~2.7) versus $12.25B on a pure time-shift of the old path; bull $19.0B, bear $11.2B. Evidence: NYMEX front-month 3:2:1 crack averaged ~$66 in Q3-26 (PSX composite $60.17, realized $38.00), $60.7 in October, $45 in November to date and ~$41 on the valuation date - still roughly twice a normal level but fading fast, which is the path the October base narrative described; (3) capex years 1-3 lifted by ~$0.3B/0.4B/0.27B: the Q3 10-Q says 2027 capex will EXCEED the ~$2.5B target after the Western Gateway pipeline FID (49.9% of a 1,300-mile products system) - amount not yet disclosed, so the uplift is a judgment, and no EBITDA from the project is modelled (a deliberate conservatism worth ~-$2/share); (4) new equity-bridge deduction of $1.1B for the Q3-26 working-capital inflow (mostly accrued income taxes on the windfall: accrued income and other taxes 2,687 vs 1,362 at Dec-25) that sits in 30-Sep cash but is payable - at the June anchor H1 working capital was neutral (-21), so no such item was needed then. UNCHANGED (stated, not silent): mid-cycle EBITDA ~$10.4B base / ~$13B bull / ~$7.5B bear from year 3 (anchor: Q3/Q4-25 at ~$12/bbl realized = ~$9.6B annualised + Midstream to $4.5B run-rate by YE2027 + CPChem 2027 start-ups); one super-cycle quarter does not move a through-cycle margin - evidence that would: FY2027 capacity-closure data or two consecutive post-normalisation quarters with realized margins holding above ~$14/bbl (up) or below ~$10/bbl (down). Also unchanged: later-year growth 2-2.5%, SBC ~0.16% of revenue, cash tax 23% (FY25 cash tax of $200M and 9M-26 deferred tax of $375M are timing, not a lower structural rate), D&A ~1.72% (Q3-26 $591M confirms the ~$2.35B run-rate), wc_capture 0, WACC 9%, terminal growth, 14x cap, 25/50/25 weights, NCI $1.7B. Revenue is price-driven; the path falls from the inflated LTM ($168B at WTI ~$86 in Q3) toward ~$137B and the margin path is set so revenue x margin hits the EBITDA dollars. Interest income not stripped (net debt company). Total debt target $17B by YE2027 (10-Q); $492M of notes repaid from cash on 1-Oct-2026 (net-debt neutral).

bear.narrative: The November crack slide continues: Q4-26 ~$5.2B is largely banked, but offline capacity returns in early 2027 and margins revert to 2024-like ~$9/bbl (year 1 ~$11.2B); ~$7.5B mid-cycle EBITDA with Renewables loss-making again. Mid-cycle unchanged.

base.narrative: Year-1 (Oct-26 to Sep-27) EBITDA ~$14.0B: Q4-26 ~$5.5B on a crack that averaged ~$61 in October and ~$45 in November, then ~$3.0B, ~$2.8B, ~$2.7B as it fades to mid-cycle. ~$10.6B in year 2, ~$10.4B mid-cycle from year 3 growing with nominal revenue (unchanged dollars, shifted one quarter). Capex ~$2.75-2.9B in years 1-3 (Western Gateway), ~$2.5B-equivalent thereafter.

bull.narrative: Super-cycle runs through mid-2027 (year 1 ~$19.0B: ~6.0, 5.0, 4.5, 3.6 by quarter) and settles at a structurally higher ~$13B mid-cycle (~$15/bbl realized refining margin) after permanent closures. Mid-cycle unchanged.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 14x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: UNCHANGED at 25/50/25. Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25% because the valuation date is just past a refining-margin peak and mean reversion from such peaks has been the historical norm (2008, 2015, 2022-24); the bear is a return to 2024 conditions, not a solvency case. Base 50% as the evidence-weighted mid-cycle. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs several independent things to go right at once (structural margin floor, chemicals upcycle, credit-value support). Q3-2026 was stronger than any scenario assumed, but the November crack slide is the reversion the bear weight exists for; neither moves the odds on the mid-cycle level.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
